rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read
rules_evaluated.evidence: Re-derived from scratch. The prior-instance defect is fixed: chunk 5 line 51 now reads 'the soft item (the step that reads clean but skips over something)' — the definite article is justified by an inline parenthetical gloss at the very first use, same bullet, same slide (not deferred to the next slide as before). Checked every other definite-article/pronoun use under the sequential read: chunk 5's 'the agent's walk-down' self-glosses two sentences later in the same bullet ('it can walk every unresolved branch of the decision tree...'); chunk 6's 'candidates' (line 59) is exemplified in the same bullet ('That answer is a candidate'); chunk 6's reuse of 'a soft item' (indefinite article) correctly points back at chunk 5's now-established term; chunk 7's 'the read' / 'the branches' correctly reuse terms chunk 5 established ('your read', 'decision tree'). Chunk 2 line 31 'Skip if you trust the framing' resolves against chunk 1's account of what plan mode is (permission state / read-only) — a plausible single antecedent, not left ambiguous holding prior chunks. The new 2026-08-08 deferral bullet (chunk 7, lines 65) introduces 'mid-run' (arc-earned spine vocabulary, session/task/run per curriculum/vocabulary.md) and 'A wrong call' / 'it' which resolve within the same bullet. No never-named or stranded referents found.

No 'the opening lecture said...' style positional callback to another file anywhere in body. Chunk 2 line 31's 'The exercise will show you either way' names no file and makes no content claim about it; verified against curriculum/trainings/agentic-engineering-101/plan-mode-done-right.md ## Start here, where 'Exercise: Push back on the plan' is the single exercise immediately following this lecture — unambiguous under the module's one-exercise-per-module architecture, functioning as navigation/promise rather than a narrative claim requiring positional disambiguation.

Verified counts against literal header claims: 'Five things a good plan has' has exactly 5 bulleted criteria (file list / early runnable slice / verification step / named assumptions / non-goals); 'Three pressures that make bad plans look good' has exactly 3 (structure / reasonableness / agreement). All other headers ('Plan mode is a read-only permission state', 'Two reads, paired', 'Find is easier than judge', 'Plan review is a high-leverage gate') are borne out by their chunk content, including the new deferral bullet, which supports rather than contradicts 'high-leverage gate' by showing the cost of skipping it.

Grepped and read the full body for each sub-tic: no 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' construction (the sole 'Not' hit at line 35 is ordinary contrastive prose inside one bullet, not the banned triple); no anaphora/epistrophe triples; no self-grading superlative (grep for 'one of the most/most useful/most valuable' returns zero body hits — the only match is inside the exempt backing block citing Osmani); no number-with-retraction pattern; the one abstraction-noun candidate, chunk 7's 'the wrongness tangles with everything built after it', is immediately cashed out concretely in the same sentence ('what would have been a line edit in the plan becomes an untangling job in the code'), satisfying the rule's own remedy inline; no verb triplet with an empty leg (only two-verb pairs joined by 'and', which don't trigger the 3-leg test).
